paras: The killing of John Franklin was the fatal shooting of a Black prisoner by City Marshal John Way in a cell of the jail at South Charleston, Ohio, on the night of December 25, 1882. Way said Franklin attacked him when he entered the cell, and that account, from a single dispatch, was printed across the country among the season's 'Christmas crimes'.
Franklin, described in the dispatches as 'colored', had been arrested in South Charleston on Christmas Day for disorderly conduct and was held in the town jail.

That night the marshal entered Franklin's cell. According to the dispatch sent from South Charleston to the Cincinnati Commercial, Franklin 'made a vicious attack' on Way, and the marshal shot him dead on the spot. No other witness or version of what happened in the cell appears in the coverage.
No report of an inquest, arrest or charge against the marshal was found in the coverage, which ends within five days of the shooting.

The story reached readers through a Cincinnati dispatch quoting the Commercial's South Charleston special, which ran on December 26 in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer under the head 'A Way Out', in the New-York Tribune, and in the Saint Paul Daily Globe as 'Shot a Prisoner'. Most papers set it among lists of holiday shootings and stabbings, as in the Washington Evening Star's 'The Christmas Killed and Wounded' and the Daily Gazette's 'Christmas Crimes'. The Richmond Dispatch repeated the wire text on December 28, and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union named South Charleston, Ohio in an editorial blaming the season's murders on drink.

Nearly every version printed the marshal's account as fact. Shorter items sharpened it: the Stark County Democrat of Canton, Ohio called Franklin 'a vicious colored prisoner', and the Bismarck Tribune, without naming him, wrote of 'a vicious negro' who made 'a savage attack'. The Ottawa Free Trader alone marked the claim as the marshal's own, writing that 'Way says' Franklin attacked him. No Black-press coverage from 1882 is available for comparison.

Copying errors spread the story to the wrong places: the Evening Star located it in 'Charleston. S. C.', and the Fremont County Record of Colorado placed it in 'South Charleston, Kentucky' and named the marshal 'Joseph N. Way'. The original dispatch, filed from South Charleston, Ohio, gives the marshal's name as John Way.

accounts.label: Marshal's claim, as attributed

framing.detail: Most papers ran the Commercial special nearly verbatim inside Christmas crime roundups, under heads such as 'A Way Out' and 'Shot a Prisoner'.
Condensed versions called Franklin 'a vicious colored prisoner' and 'a vicious negro' who made 'a savage attack'.
The Ottawa Free Trader wrote that 'Way says' Franklin attacked him; the Sacramento Record-Union listed the town among Christmas murder reports.

conflicts.note: The source dispatch was filed to the Cincinnati Commercial from South Charleston, Ohio (A5); the other states are copying errors.
Only a distant Colorado roundup gives Joseph N.; the wire text says John.
